beats.text: Your friends have more friends than you. That's math, not you!
Picture one very popular person. Lots of people count them as a friend.
So whenever people look at their friends, that person shows up again and again. And the average goes up.
A sociologist checked this in a high school. And here's what he found.
Most students had fewer friends than their friends! Fifty-five percent of the girls.
So if everyone seems more social than you: that's an illusion. Not a you problem.

ask: SEND THIS TO A FRIEND. THEY HAVE MORE.
sources: Feld (1991), Why your friends have more friends than you do, American Journal of Sociology 96(6), 1464–1477 – the 'friendship paradox': popular people appear in many friend lists, so the mean number of friends of friends exceeds the mean number of friends; in Coleman's Marketville high-school data 80 of 146 girls (55%) had fewer friends than the mean of their friends, 41 had more, 25 the same; mean 2.7 friends vs 3.4 for friends.
